solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A custom to stop walk, needing time for a snack

indicators.note: to stop something up is to plug it, so the custom phrase goes into the middle of the walk
needing here means lacking, so the walk word goes without its time letter

parts.note: a stroll is a leisurely walk
a usage is an established custom or practice

explanation.surface: Someone halts a stroll by tradition because they need time to grab a bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing time' reads as wanting more time, but here it means STROLL lacks its T, leaving SROLL, which A USAGE then plugs.
explanation.definitionFit: This pastry-wrapped meat item is a classic British savoury bite eaten between meals.

clue.text: Discovered fattish, round, family of nuthatches

indicators.note: turned round, the remaining letters are read backwards
dis-covered means with the covering stripped, so the outer letters of the word fattish go

explanation.surface: A plump bird is spotted, perched among a family of nuthatches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' strips FATTISH to ATTIS; 'round' turns that into SITTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitta is the scientific grouping (strictly the genus) into which ornithologists place the nuthatch birds.

clue.text: Raising up one foot in 17A, relieving pressure

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the one-and-foot pair inside the other word
relieving it of pressure takes that letter away from the cross-referenced word

parts.note: the answer to 17 Across, a word for an exclamation mark
P is the physics symbol for pressure
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A physiotherapy note: lifting one foot, with weight eased off, while doing exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 17A is an exclamation mark's jargon name; 'relieving pressure' removes its P before 'in' takes the one-and-foot letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplifting is a lifting or elevating action, so it matches raising as a gerund or participle.

clue.text: Apart from the best single?

definitions.meaning: set to one side, away from the rest
the main track of a record release, the one meant to be the hit, as opposed to its flip side

explanation.surface: A question about what lies beyond the top-selling record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apart from' reads as one phrase meaning except, but 'from' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Aside means apart or to one side; an A-side is the lead track of a vinyl single.

clue.text: Tackle English chaps about Sally Traffic's origin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the English-and-chaps pair wraps around the sally

parts.note: chaps are men
a sally is a witty remark, a quip

indicators.note: a word's origin is its first letter

explanation.surface: Fishing gear is handed over by Englishmen talking about a traffic reporter named Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name but is a witty remark; 'Traffic's origin' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear or apparatus for a job, especially fishing, a general synonym for kit.

clue.text: Old relative has left out cat

indicators.note: left out means the letter for left is removed from the relative

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

explanation.surface: An elderly family member has put the cat outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as one phrase about the cat; 'out' takes L from UNCLE, giving UNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big wild feline of Central Asia.

clue.text: Spur on one who insists something very smelly will result

parts.note: a spur is an offshoot or branch, as is a limb
someone who urges or presses a point is an urger

explanation.surface: Encouraging a stubborn person will produce a stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spur' reads as a verb but is a noun for a branch; 'on' simply puts URGER after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a Belgian soft cheese famous for its strong pungent odour.

clue.text: Primate's right-hand man (of the cross) shunning judge

parts.note: RH is the standard abbreviation for right hand

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the judge letter is dropped

parts.note: Jesus is the man crucified on the cross

explanation.surface: An archbishop's trusted aide, a churchman, keeps away from the judiciary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests a senior bishop, but it is the animal sense; JESUS less J gives ESUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey, a member of the order of mammals that includes apes and humans.

clue.text: Draft law against something that's mostly base

parts.note: a bill is a proposed law put before parliament
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: A proposed statute opposes something largely without principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks moral but means base metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Billon is an alloy of silver or gold with a majority of cheaper base metal, used in coinage.

clue.text: The Oldie circulated by University Hospital

indicators.note: circulated means sent round, so the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: The Oldie magazine is distributed around a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British humour magazine; its letters THEOLDIE rearrange to HOTELDIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hôtel-Dieu is the traditional French name for a town's main charitable infirmary, literally God's house.

clue.text: Dark things finally changed one who'd prefer others to suffer?

indicators.note: finally changed means the last letter is swapped for another

parts.words: one who'd prefer others to suffer?
parts.note: a nimby objects to development near home, happy for it to be elsewhere

explanation.surface: Bleak happenings at last altered a person who wishes misery on others.
explanation.walkthrough: NIMBY (not in my back yard) has its final Y changed to I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi, the plural of nimbus, are grey rain clouds, which darken the sky.

clue.text: Steal inferior silver, regularly hidden for fencing

indicators.note: one piece is hidden, the other acts as fencing around it
regularly picks every other letter of the word silver

parts.note: naff is British slang for inferior or tacky

explanation.surface: A thief pinches cheap silverware and stashes it to sell to a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like receiving stolen goods but means surrounding; SLE surrounds NAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is informal British for to take or pinch something, especially quickly.

clue.text: Possibly book in advance before getting left out in crush

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: left out means the letter for left is removed

parts.note: to quell is to crush or suppress

explanation.surface: Reserving ahead to avoid being excluded in a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book in advance' reads as reserve; it is a book set in advance of an existing story.
explanation.definitionFit: A prequel is a story, such as a novel, whose events come earlier than an existing work.

clue.text: Trap sponger?

parts.note: trap is slang for the mouth, and this table napkin is what wipes it clean

explanation.surface: A con artist who lives off others gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'; 'sponger' becomes something that sponges or wipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A table napkin is used at meals to dab the lips clean, so it sponges the mouth.

clue.text: 10 can lead to such hard times to come

definitions.meaning: the answer to 10 Across, rain clouds, bring wet weather
future periods of need, as in saving for them

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is NIMBI, rain clouds, which bring wet days.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving for a rainy day means putting money by for future hardship; literally they are wet days.

clue.text: Dogged by extremely unspeakable actions following representation

indicators.note: a representation presents the letters in another form, a fresh arrangement
extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Being hounded by unspeakably vile deeds after someone's portrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' reads as harassed but means persistent; the outer UE of 'unspeakable' joins ACTIONS for the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged as an adjective means stubbornly persistent, never letting go.

clue.text: Infidel beginning to practise once more after I left

indicators.note: after places the shortened word after the first letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter
left here means departed, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A non-believer starts going to worship again after the speaker quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' reads as the speaker departing, but it tells you to drop the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagan, like infidel, is a term for a person who rejects the dominant religion.

clue.text: Cast kept entertaining sudden great demand before a popular ballet

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so one part goes inside the other
cast means thrown or formed anew, so the letters of kept are rearranged

parts.note: a rush is a sudden surge of demand

explanation.surface: A theatre company held a crowd-pulling ballet in huge demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a troupe but rearranges KEPT into PETK, which holds RUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrushka is Stravinsky's 1911 ballet for the Ballets Russes, still widely performed.

clue.text: Somewhat Kiplingesque!

indicators.note: somewhat means part of, so the letters come from inside the word

explanation.surface: A remark that something is a bit like Kipling's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark itself is the definition; pling is a hacker's name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pling is jargon among programmers for the exclamation point punctuation symbol.

clue.text: Short leisurely walk around terrace, empty for now

indicators.note: around means surrounding the other part

parts.note: prom is short for promenade, a leisurely walk

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A quick stroll past a deserted row of houses, just for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' signals the abbreviation of promenade, a seaside walkway; 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of 'terrace'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem, from Latin pro tempore, means temporarily.

clue.text: Pools win ultimately leads to a tiara being ordered

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word
being ordered means being put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A football pools win eventually lets someone order a tiara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pools' suggests the football pools, the British betting game on match results; it is swimming pools.
explanation.definitionFit: Natatoria, plural of natatorium, are indoor swimming baths.

clue.text: All points in annual return are what is 23

indicators.note: in places the points inside the abbreviation

parts.note: AR is the abbreviation for annual return
all the compass points are north, south, west and east

explanation.surface: Every item in a yearly filing is what is given as a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is CLUED; the answer is what a clue is written for.
explanation.definitionFit: What a crossword clue leads to is the solution that fills the grid.

clue.text: It may precede record of compliancy formed after withdrawal of Congress

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new word after taking out those of the other piece

parts.note: the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: A record of compliance made after a congressional pull-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, N, C from COMPLIANCY and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympic record is the best performance set at the Games, so the adjective precedes the noun.

clue.text: Advertising for a brief period

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a mo is informal for a moment

explanation.surface: Advertisements run only for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is promotional publicity, such as a trailer for a product.

clue.text: Swoops on pimps outside community centre

indicators.note: outside means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: ponces is British slang for pimps

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Police raid procurers operating around a local hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'community centre' reads as a building but gives the middle letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoop on something is to pounce on it, attacking suddenly.

clue.text: Scrap that may follow cross work conversation?

definitions.text: that may follow cross work conversation?
definitions.meaning: the word completes crossbar-style beam, piecework and a talking-point object

explanation.surface: A question about a fight that might come after a tense office exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes after 'cross' and 'conversation' and before 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a bit or fragment of something, as a scrap is.

clue.text: What every setter did — went to pot around fifty

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps the other

parts.note: in snooker, a player cued to pot a ball
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Every compiler fell apart around the age of fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went to pot' reads as declined but means used a cue to pot a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter writes hints for each entry; the past tense fits 'did'.

clue.text: Muse album's first to follow Queen

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, placing the later pieces behind the royal letters

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A rock band's album opens with a Queen song.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was the Greek goddess who inspired lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Hospitality of public audience

parts.note: open means public, available to all
a house is a theatre audience

explanation.surface: A welcome extended to the general public.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means offering a welcome to all callers.

clue.text: Representative reset the password

indicators.note: reset means set again in a different order

explanation.surface: A union official changed the computer login.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop steward is a union official elected to represent workers.
